faq.title: Everything About
faq.subtitle: How disposable email works here - and exactly what happens to your data.
faq.question1: What is a temporary email or temp mail?
faq.answer1: A temporary email (also called temp mail, disposable email, or throwaway email) is a self-destructing email address that you can use for a short period. It helps protect your real email from spam, phishing, and unwanted marketing emails when signing up for websites or services.
faq.answer2: Disposable email works by providing you with a random email address instantly. Any emails sent to this address appear in your temporary inbox in real-time. After a set period (typically 10 minutes), the email address and all received messages are automatically deleted.
faq.question3: Is temp mail safe to use?
faq.answer3: Yes, temp mail is safe to use for non-sensitive purposes like signing up for websites, downloading resources, or testing applications. However, you should never use temporary email for important accounts like banking, as the emails will be deleted and you may lose access.
faq.question4: How long does a temporary email last?
faq.answer4: By default an inbox lasts 10 minutes. Anyone can extend it to 1 hour or 24 hours; with a free account you can extend up to 30 days or save the address as a permanent mailbox that is kept until you delete it.
faq.answer5: Some websites maintain blocklists of known temporary email domains. While TempMail Central uses multiple domains to minimize this, some strict websites may still detect and block temporary email addresses.
faq.question6: Do I need to register to use temp mail?
faq.answer6: No registration is required to use TempMail Central. Simply visit the website and you will automatically receive a temporary email address that you can use immediately.
faq.question7: Can I receive attachments with temp mail?
faq.answer7: Yes. Attachments can be viewed and downloaded while the inbox is active. Each inbox keeps its most recent 100 messages.
faq.question8: What is temp mail used for?
faq.answer8: Temp mail is commonly used for: signing up for free trials, avoiding spam from newsletters, testing email functionality in applications, protecting your real email from data breaches, online shopping on untrusted sites, and accessing one-time downloads or resources.
faq.question9: Who can read a temporary inbox?
faq.answer9: While it is active, anyone who knows the exact address can open it - there is no password. Protection comes from the address being one of 3.6 quadrillion combinations and from its short lifetime. Never send sensitive information to a temporary address; permanent mailboxes are private to your account.
faq.question10: What data does TempMail Central keep?
faq.answer10: Temporary mail lives in memory and is erased at expiry. Beyond that: daily aggregate counters, 14-day web server logs, and account data if you register. No visitor profiles, no analytics trackers, no selling data - the details are in our Privacy Policy.

tech.title: How TempMail Central Actually Works
tech.subtitle: No black box: this is exactly what happens to an address and its mail, from creation to deletion.

generation.title: Address generation
generation.description: Ten lowercase letters and digits from a cryptographically secure random source - about 3.6 quadrillion possible addresses. Operational prefixes like admin@ or support@ are never issued.

storage.title: Storage & deletion
storage.description: Temporary inboxes live in Redis, an in-memory store, with a countdown attached. When it hits zero the address and every message are evicted - no archives, no backups, no recovery.

delivery.title: Real-time delivery
delivery.description: Our Postfix mail server accepts the message, a parser hands it to the app, and a WebSocket pushes it into your open tab - usually within a second or two of the sender hitting send.

limits.title: Attachments & limits
limits.description: Attachments can be viewed and downloaded while the inbox is active. Each inbox keeps its most recent 100 messages, and addresses are receive-only - nothing can ever be sent from them.

logging.title: What we log
logging.description: Daily totals (inboxes created, mail received), plus standard web server logs kept for 14 days. No analytics trackers, no visitor profiles, and personal data is never sold.

abuse.title: Abuse prevention
abuse.description: Per-IP rate limits, reserved service prefixes, and account bans keep misuse in check - and account sign-ups with throwaway addresses are refused, so registered users stay reachable.

tech.more: Want more depth? The blog covers the deletion mechanics, address entropy, and abuse handling in detail.
